To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The ordinary kriging method is not suitable for soil nutrient element prediction in the tobacco planting region of Chongqing, China, because of its high spatial heterogeneity.
the coregionalized ordinary kriging (COK) is an effective method for predicting soil nutrient elements using ancillary terrain data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a new prediction method to improve the accuracy of soil nutrient elements prediction in tobacco planting regions.
the prediction of soil nutrient elements (N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S, Zn, Mn, Fe, Cu, B, and Al) in Chongqing tobacco planting region, China.

the following questions: (1) how to predict the spatial distribution of soil nutrient elements in tobacco planting region using the ancillary terrain data and (2) how to evaluate the performance of the predictions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ancillary terrain data can be used as auxiliary variables in spatial prediction to improve the prediction accuracy, especially for the sparse soil data.
the spatial prediction of soil properties is not only a function of the variogram, but also a function of the ancillary data used to predict.
the spatial interpolation of soil nutrients using ancillary terrain data has been proved to be an effective method to predict the spatial variation of soil properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the soil nutrient elements are not only spatially correlated but also correlated with DEM and Landsat TM data.
the soil data are coregionized with the DEM data, and the coregionalized soil data are used to predict soil properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ancillary variables can be used to increase prediction accuracy of soil nutrient status.

, in a region where the soil data are sparse, the use of ancillary data to improve the accuracy of the predictions of the soil nutrient elements is effective, especially for the spatial prediction of phosphorus.
the coregionalization approach can be used to predict soil nutrient properties at places between sampling points, which is a more effective method than ordinary kriging when the data are sparse.
